For easier interpretation, here are the parameters, and the resulting delta score for SALib 1.4.5 and SALib 1.5.1, and I have added the Pearson correlation with the output parameter as well. Will attach the full Si returned by delta.analyze() at the end for reference as well.

Things to note (indicated in colour):

GREEN Disproportionately reduced delta scores in v1.5.1. Note how param05 had the highest delta value in v1.4.5. In v1.5.1, it has less than 50% of the delta score of the highest parameter (param01). (and delta of param01 is largely unaffected)
PINK Delta scores have not changed much. However, because the green parameters have been reduced by so much, they now appear much more important than the green parameters in v1.5.1, whereas, in v1.4.5, they were insignificant compared to the green parameters.
BLUE This parameter was one of the most significant in v1.4.5, and is now almost insignificant compared to other parameters in v1.5.1.

Relationships and nature of the parameters:

GREEN These parameters have some correlation among each other (similar properties and behaviour) and param02-param09 have many zero-values (related to solar radiation over 24-hours)
PINK These parameters are highly correlated with the output parameter, as well as the param01 (which has the highest delta score).
BLUE This parameter has many zero-values, and its relationship with the output parameter is suspected to be a step-like input. However, the result does not change when I use only the non-zero values in the input data, or if I normalize the input set differently (binary (1 or 0) inputs, or logarithmically). I am unable to replicate its high delta score in v1.4.5, no matter how I format the input, or tweak y_resamples in 1.5.1.

Any help or input would be appreciated, as to which of these results are the most reliable.
My greatest concern is that the delta values are not changed for all parameters, only a select few (green and blue, 10 out of 22 inputs). This makes input parameters ranking order in terms of importance very different - and greatly affects the interpretation and spread of relative importance.
The results from v1.4.5 make more sense to me, but I do want to know what the most correct answer is.
Note on zero-values: The parameters which have the most substantial change from v1.4.5 to v1.5.1 all have quite a few zero-values. However, changing the scaling methods (binary, logarithmic) or resampling using only entries with non-zero values for those parameters, does not affect it to nearly the same extent to achieve similar values to that in v1.4.5.

I have a remark with regards to SaLib, namely in the Section on Sobol’ Sensitivity Analysis it says: “Saltelli’s scheme extends the Sobol’ sequence in a way to reduce the error rates in the resulting sensitivity index calculations”. Saltelli indeed proposed a formula to reduce the number of model runs from N ( 2D +1) to N(D+1) ( it was also published at the same time in [1]) but it was I who proposed a formula to reduce the error rates in the resulting sensitivity index calculations. [1] Mauntz W. Global sensitivity analysis of general nonlinear systems. Master’s thesis, Imperial College London, CPSE; 2002. [Supervisors: C. Pantelides and S. Kucherenko.].

[3] S. Kucherenko, S. Song, Different numerical estimators for main effect global sensitivity indices. Reliability Engineering and System Safety, 165 (2017) 222-238

nodes.bodyText:
I use a fairly large pre-generated sample set and use the Delta Moment-Independent Analysis for global sensitivity indices. I want to use only a subset of samples for estimation of delta and S1 indices and the bootstrap estimation of their confidence intervals. Therefore, I have introduced a new Parameter 'Nr' into the routines. Another minor improvement is an switch to deselect additional estimation of first-order sobol indices. As I have trouble creating a fork and a pull request, I attach my code in the hope, that on of you maintainer might merge it into the code base.
from typing import Dict
from scipy.stats import norm, gaussian_kde, rankdata

import numpy as np

from . import common_args
from ..util import read_param_file, ResultDict


def analyze(
    problem: Dict,
    X: np.ndarray,
    Y: np.ndarray,
    num_resamples: int = 100,
    conf_level: float = 0.95,
    print_to_console: bool = False,
    seed: int = None,
    Nr: int = None,
    analyze_sobol: bool = True,
) -> Dict:
    """Perform Delta Moment-Independent Analysis on model outputs.

    Returns a dictionary with keys 'delta', 'delta_conf', 'S1', and 'S1_conf' 
    (first-order sobol indices), where each entry is a list of size D 
    (the number of parameters) containing the indices in the same order as the 
    parameter file. 


    Notes
    -----
    Compatible with:
        all samplers


    Examples
    --------
        >>> X = latin.sample(problem, 1000)
        >>> Y = Ishigami.evaluate(X)
        >>> Si = delta.analyze(problem, X, Y, print_to_console=True)


    Parameters
    ----------
    problem : dict
        The problem definition
    X: numpy.matrix
        A NumPy matrix containing the model inputs
    Y : numpy.array
        A NumPy array containing the model outputs
    num_resamples : int
        The number of resamples when computing confidence intervals (default 100)
    conf_level : float
        The confidence interval level (default 0.95)
    print_to_console : bool
        Print results directly to console (default False)
    Nr: int
        Number of samples to use when resampling (bootstrap) (default None)
    analyze_sobol: int
        Also compute first-order sobol indices and their confidence intervals (default True)


    References
    ----------
    1. Borgonovo, E. (2007). "A new uncertainty importance measure."
           Reliability Engineering & System Safety, 92(6):771-784,
           doi:10.1016/j.ress.2006.04.015.

    2. Plischke, E., E. Borgonovo, and C. L. Smith (2013). "Global
           sensitivity measures from given data." European Journal of
           Operational Research, 226(3):536-550, doi:10.1016/j.ejor.2012.11.047.
    """
    if seed:
        np.random.seed(seed)

    D = problem["num_vars"]
    if Nr is None:
        Nr = Y.size

    if not 0 < conf_level < 1:
        raise RuntimeError("Confidence level must be between 0-1.")

    # equal frequency partition
    exp = 2.0 / (7.0 + np.tanh((1500.0 - Nr) / 500.0))
    M = int(np.round(min(int(np.ceil(Nr**exp)), 48)))
    m = np.linspace(0, Nr, M + 1)
    Ygrid = np.linspace(np.min(Y), np.max(Y), 100)

    keys = ("delta", "delta_conf", "S1", "S1_conf")
    S = ResultDict((k, np.zeros(D)) for k in keys)
    S["names"] = problem["names"]

    try:
        for i in range(D):
            X_i = X[:, i]
            S["delta"][i], S["delta_conf"][i] = bias_reduced_delta(
                Y, Ygrid, X_i, m, num_resamples, conf_level, Nr
            )
            if analyze_sobol:
                ind = np.random.randint(Y.size, size=Nr)
                S["S1"][i] = sobol_first(Y[ind], X_i[ind], m)
                S["S1_conf"][i] = sobol_first_conf(Y, X_i, m, num_resamples, conf_level, Nr)
    except np.linalg.LinAlgError as e:
        msg = "Singular matrix detected\n"
        msg += "This may be due to the sample size ({}) being too small\n".format(
            Y.size
        )
        msg += "If this is not the case, check Y values or raise an issue with the\n"
        msg += "SALib team"

        raise np.linalg.LinAlgError(msg) from e

    if print_to_console:
        print(S.to_df())

    return S


def calc_delta(Y, Ygrid, X, m):
    """Plischke et al. (2013) delta index estimator (eqn 26) for d_hat."""
    N = len(Y)
    fy = gaussian_kde(Y, bw_method="silverman")(Ygrid)
    xr = rankdata(X, method="ordinal")

    d_hat = 0.0
    l_m = len(m) - 1
    for j in range(l_m):
        ix = np.where((xr > m[j]) & (xr <= m[j + 1]))[0]
        nm = len(ix)

        # if not np.all(np.equal(Y_ix, Y_ix[0])):
        Y_ix = Y[ix]
        if Y_ix.ptp() != 0.0:
            fyc = gaussian_kde(Y_ix, bw_method="silverman")(Ygrid)
            fy_ = np.abs(fy - fyc)
        else:
            fy_ = np.abs(fy)

        d_hat += (nm / (2 * N)) * np.trapz(fy_, Ygrid)

    return d_hat


def bias_reduced_delta(Y, Ygrid, X, m, num_resamples, conf_level, Nr):
    """Plischke et al. 2013 bias reduction technique (eqn 30)"""
    d = np.empty(num_resamples)

    N = len(Y)
    if Nr is None: 
        Nr = N
    ind = np.random.randint(N, size=Nr)
    d_hat = calc_delta(Y[ind], Ygrid, X[ind], m)
    r = np.random.randint(N, size=(num_resamples, Nr))
    for i in range(num_resamples):
        r_i = r[i, :]
        d[i] = calc_delta(Y[r_i], Ygrid, X[r_i], m)

    d = 2.0 * d_hat - d
    return (d.mean(), norm.ppf(0.5 + conf_level / 2) * d.std(ddof=1))


def sobol_first(Y, X, m):
    # pre-process to catch constant array
    # see: https://github.com/numpy/numpy/issues/9631
    if Y.ptp() == 0.0:
        # Catch constant results
        # If Y does not change then it is not sensitive to anything...
        return 0.0

    xr = rankdata(X, method="ordinal")
    Vi = 0
    N = len(Y)
    Y_mean = Y.mean()
    for j in range(len(m) - 1):
        ix = np.where((xr > m[j]) & (xr <= m[j + 1]))[0]
        nm = len(ix)
        Vi += (nm / N) * ((Y[ix].mean() - Y_mean) ** 2)

    return Vi / np.var(Y)


def sobol_first_conf(Y, X, m, num_resamples, conf_level, Nr):
    s = np.zeros(num_resamples)

    N = len(Y)
    if Nr is None: 
        Nr = N
    r = np.random.randint(N, size=(num_resamples, Nr))
    for i in range(num_resamples):
        r_i = r[i, :]
        s[i] = sobol_first(Y[r_i], X[r_i], m)

    return norm.ppf(0.5 + conf_level / 2) * s.std(ddof=1)


def cli_parse(parser):
    parser.add_argument(
        "-X",
        "--model-input-file",
        type=str,
        required=True,
        default=None,
        help="Model input file",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "-r",
        "--resamples",
        type=int,
        required=False,
        default=10,
        help="Number of bootstrap resamples for \
                           Sobol confidence intervals",
    )
    return parser


def cli_action(args):
    problem = read_param_file(args.paramfile)
    Y = np.loadtxt(
        args.model_output_file, delimiter=args.delimiter, usecols=(args.column,)
    )
    X = np.loadtxt(args.model_input_file, delimiter=args.delimiter, ndmin=2)
    if len(X.shape) == 1:
        X = X.reshape((len(X), 1))

    analyze(
        problem,
        X,
        Y,
        num_resamples=args.resamples,
        print_to_console=True,
        seed=args.seed,
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    common_args.run_cli(cli_parse, cli_action)

Problem
In the Wrapping an Existing Model documentation, it is stated that "[The SALib ProblemSpec Interface] automatically applies the model for each individual sample set in a for loop (at the cost of computational efficiency)". However, this does not appear to be the case.
From the "problem.py" file:
def evaluate(self, func, *args, **kwargs):
    if "nprocs" in kwargs:
        nprocs = kwargs.pop("nprocs")
        return self.evaluate_parallel(func, *args, nprocs=nprocs, **kwargs)

    self.results = func(self._samples, *args, **kwargs)
    return self
It appears, from this method, that func is simply called with the full matrix of samples as the first argument. The parallel version breaks the matrix into chunks (sub-matrices) and passes those chunks as the first argument.
Suggestion
I think you might want to edit the document to better represent the true functionality of ProblemSpec.evaluate(), unless my assessment is incorrect.
Perhaps you could clarify that if the user wants to utilize the parallel functionality for a model that is "not [easily] expressed in a vectorizable form", the wrapper function should include a for loop. Something like:
def linear(a: float, b: float, x: float):
    return a + b * x

def wrapper(X: numpy.array, func=linear):
    results = numpy.empty(X.shape[0])
    for i in range(X.shape[0]):
        a, b, x = X[i, :]
        results[i] = func(a, b, x)
   return results

Hello,
I was trying to run the latest 1.4.0 version to perform Sobol' GSA using Saltelli method and I am not able to saltelli.sample a sequence with skip_values = 0.
I am not sure why the default skip_values is set to 1024 as later on this will for sure throw either a Warning or an Error according to how unlucky the user has been in choosing the N value.
Also, I am not sure why the default skip_values is not set to 0, as in your documentation you refer to a paper (http://arxiv.org/abs/2008.08051) where it is explicitly proved that skipping the first/firsts points of a Sobol' sequence could be deleterious.
Anyway, I had a look at the code and apparently I cannot set skip_values = 0 since the math.log operator complains when computing the m_exp exponent:
math.log(0, 2)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
ValueError: math domain error

An easy fix (although I am sure you'd like to keep using math) would be to use the numpy function as this does return something (-inf) which at least won't make the following if statement (if n_exp >= m_exp) fail:
np.log2(0)
<stdin>:1: RuntimeWarning: divide by zero encountered in log2
-inf

Thanks a lot!
